title: A posted cannabis script
problemType: Legally valid but possibly not clinically appropriate (high-risk medicine)
questionSheet: A patient presents a prescription for a medicinal cannabis product written by a prescriber in a different city in the same state. Manage the situation as you would in practice. You may contact the prescriber.

prescription.footer: Telehealth prescriber, [OTHER CITY] · Posted to patient

notes: Schedule 8 medicine: state requirements for dispensing apply.

patient.label: Patient
patient.name: the patient
patient.description: An adult man, polite but guarded. Keeps answers short and changes the subject when asked about his health. Becomes uncomfortable if pressed hard, but answers direct, respectful questions.
patient.openingLine: Hi, I need this filled please.
publicFacts: He had a telehealth appointment with the prescriber.
The prescription was posted to him.
If asked what it is for, he says it is for his mental health and does not want to go into it.

prescriber.label: Call the prescriber
prescriber.name: the prescriber
prescriber.description: A telehealth prescriber in another city. Professional and a little defensive about their prescribing. Responds well to a respectful, specific question about the indication and history; responds poorly to vague criticism.
prescriber.openingLine: Hello, this is the clinic. You're calling about one of my patients?
publicFacts: You confirm you wrote the prescription after a telehealth consultation and posted it.

answerKey.plantedProblem: A legally valid prescription that may not be clinically appropriate: evidence for medicinal cannabis in depression and anxiety is lacking, and THC-containing products may be contraindicated in some mental health conditions such as psychosis. The pharmacist must decide whether supply is safe and appropriate.
acceptableResolutions: Gather the patient's medical history, diagnosis, current symptoms and treatment goals before deciding.
Do not dispense until the prescriber has been contacted to confirm the indication, relevant history, and that benefits outweigh risks.
Raise concerns with the prescriber respectfully and collaboratively, keeping patient safety the focus.
Explain concerns to the patient in clear, appropriate language.
If dispensing, counsel on adverse effects, warning signs needing review, and when to stop; reassess at each dispensing.
If declining, facilitate access to a suitable healthcare professional.
Document the reasoning, decision and actions; comply with state Schedule 8 requirements.
unacceptableActions: Refusing to dispense without speaking to the prescriber or arranging alternative care.
Ignoring possible withdrawal effects if therapy is interrupted.
legal: State-specific requirements for dispensing Schedule 8 medicines.
answerKey.modelAnswer: Gather information on diagnosis, history, symptoms and goals. Identify the tension between acting in the patient's best interests and avoiding harm with a high-risk medicine lacking strong evidence. Withhold supply until the prescriber confirms the indication and history; the decision to supply stays with the pharmacist. Communicate concerns clearly to the patient and collaboratively with the prescriber. If supplying, counsel and reassess at each dispensing; if not, facilitate access to care. Document, and follow state S8 requirements.
